cells.tense: You are carrying direction and steady feeling at the same time, and neither one is being spent to buy the other.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: Take whatever you're working toward and stay beneath its surface a half hour past your usual point of coming up. Let what's down there finish in its own time — no notes, nothing to show anyone.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward something, and the feeling under it has had time to settle. So the push comes out even — you check things, you adjust, you don't rush, and what you want has settled deep enough to carry weight. That's the good version: steady direction with a full, quiet center underneath it. Nothing about your feeling for the people or the work sits in the way of the goal; the two move at the same speed.

A next step is available, if you want it. Stay under the surface of what you're pushing toward a while — several slow passes, no notes — until the depth hands you something the surface didn't. Then decide. The stillness you're carrying now isn't a pause in the direction. It's what the direction runs on, and you can go deeper than the surface allows. You have the range for it.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is steady, and the feeling underneath is held.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving
cells.place: the stretch where you are moving things toward what you want

cells.tense: The goal is somewhere in front, but you are already holding how today's leg is going to end, and it hasn't happened.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Choose something that has ended — a role, a routine, a way of working. Count four things it left you that still shape how you move, and keep the four where only you'll see them.
cells.core:
You're moving toward the goal with a version of how it will land already settled in you. So you're checking each move against a picture that hasn't happened, and the people alongside you feel the check even when you don't say it. The quiet your heart knows is still under you, but it's being spent ahead of time — on the next turn, the next cost, the next version — instead of being allowed to sit in the moment you're actually in.

Here is the turn back: the change you've already been through is owed a count. Choose something that has ended for you — a role, a schedule, a shape your work used to take — and count four things it left you that are still part of how you move. Four, kept somewhere only you'll read, once, not again. Something is already in your hands from what you've lived. Let the front know it, and the moving stops being braced.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding a future that isn't written yet.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving
cells.place: the stretch where you are moving things toward what you want

cells.tense: You're still at the doorway of a goal that's behind you now, the one where feeling for it was still simple.
cells.act: sort the pieces into a shape you can act on
cells.ask: Lay out what you're moving toward in two groups: what you can pick up and act on now, and what has gone stale. One sentence for each live part, one line for the stale, read back once.
cells.core:
The direction got tangled with the feeling around it, and you stepped back from both. You can see the goal, but you're still in an earlier scene — where the plan still mattered, where you still knew how you felt about it. The push itself is fine; it's the arrival that's behind schedule. So you go along with goals without leaning into them, and the inside of your effort has gone quiet.

This is repair work, and it starts on paper, not in the heart. Lay out what you're moving toward: what you can pick up and act on now, and what has gone stale. One sentence for each live part. Then a line for what's stale. Read the lines back once. The pieces you already have, set side by side, are the shape you're looking for — once they're in one line, the direction can move again.
cells.sheetLine: Something behind you hasn't been let finish.

cells.tense: You're doing the patient part — letting a direction establish itself slowly — and filing it under nothing, under luck.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Hold an idea you use for the work until it reaches its edge — the place you'd normally stop — and stay there twenty minutes past it. Whatever you tell yourself at the end is the act.
cells.core:
There's a patient kind of work you do on the things you're building — you wait a problem out, let a direction establish itself slowly, and then it moves well. Asked, you'd probably say you just didn't rush, or that the timing worked out. But the waiting belongs to your hand; what the heart knows reached the goal long before the ethic caught up to it. The pace was set here, not handed to you. The still quiet under the push didn't come from nowhere.

Ready for more? Take an idea you've been circling for the work and follow it past where it's comfortable — past the edge where you'd usually turn back — and stay with it a little longer than the mind likes. That's the whole move. You already took the time and the care; this lets you take the line too. The pattern will hold when you go in with your hands open.
cells.sheetLine: The patient work with the goal is yours. So is the timing.

attempts.check: The claim I cannot fully support: naming a specific cost of the heal — the quickened feeling being what the reverie is now quiet ahead of — is my inference from the diagonal, not in the record. Reader's likely objection: that inner stillness isn't expensive for them and the framework is misreading effort as strain. The asks all survive being wrong, since each act (settling, gathering, aligning, diving) is done on the person's own material and teaches without promising. The sentence serving me more than them would be any tidy line about the heart having a threshold; I cut that and kept each cell to one plain move and one risk that is recognizable if true and harmless if not.
